neighbours.label: a specific named material or fabric used as a noun or modifier (vinyl, velvet, leather, mesh, rubber, asphalt)
fire: After years in the sun, the vinyl on the old car seats had cracked.
She wore a pair of velvet gloves to the winter ball.
The jacket combines soft leather with a cotton lining.
The new road was paved with asphalt last summer.
A strip of mesh trim around the collar keeps the shirt cool.
The boots have a rubber sole that grips wet rocks.
Her wedding dress had a lace panel across the back.
The sofa was upholstered in a heavy denim fabric.
quiet: After years in the sun, the paint on the old car had faded.
She wore a pair of long gloves to the winter ball.
The jacket combines a smart cut with a warm lining.
The new road was opened to traffic last summer.
A strip of trim around the collar keeps the shirt neat.
The boots have a thick sole that grips wet rocks.
Her wedding dress had a wide panel across the back.
The sofa was upholstered in a heavy dark fabric.

notes: card only; + pole is the generic word 'matière/materia/material', and the - pole fires on concrete named materials; output suppresses 'material' itself
